Returns the builder view.

Staff with estimate.record_decline (Owner, Estimator; Office PROPOSED), on a published version, with If-Match: records that the customer declined it, with the customer's optional reason (OWN-DEC-103; audit log only). Returns the builder view.

get.description: Staff with estimate.draft (Owner, Estimator). The automatic unanswered-estimate reminder of one version (HH-EST-14, OWN-DEC-153): the configured cadence (reminders.cadences: 3 days after the version was successfully delivered), when the version was first delivered and when its reminder is due, whether a stop rule applies now (accepted, declined, expired, withdrawn, superseded, a customer response, a customer message or question reply, a recorded conversation, the project no longer open), and each of its deliveries: channel, state, when it is due or was sent, and the reason it was cancelled, suppressed, failed or waits. Staff-released drafts from before TSK-0121 are listed as history. The destination is not shown.

post.summary: Request review of an estimate draft
post.description: Staff with estimate.draft (PROPOSED mapping), on a draft, with If-Match. Marks it in review: the optional pre-publish review; it stays editable and can be published directly. Returns the builder view.

post.summary: Return an estimate in review to the draft
post.description: Staff with estimate.draft (PROPOSED mapping), on a version in review, with If-Match. Returns the builder view.

post.summary: Revise an estimate as a new version
post.description: Staff with estimate.revise (Owner, Estimator), on a version past review of an open project. Creates the next version of the same estimate as a draft, copied from this one and priced again by the server; the source version is never changed. Refused while the estimate has a version being edited, and once it has an accepted version (PROPOSED: accepted work changes through a change order). Publishing the new version supersedes the published one.

Staff with estimate.withdraw (Owner, Estimator), on a published version, with If-Match and a written reason (PROPOSED; kept in the audit log only). The version is kept as withdrawn and can no longer be accepted. Returns the builder view.

get.description: Staff with estimate.draft (Owner, Estimator). Estimates newest first, each with its latest version: number, project reference, customer name, version, state and the server-computed total (integer cents; null while the draft is incomplete). No internal cost or note.

post.summary: Share a field photo with the customer
post.description: Owner or Office (media.share_with_customer), with the version they saw. Makes one ready, internal field photo visible to the customer of its project in the Photos tab (HH-QA-05, HH-DATA-07); a quarantined, rejected or restricted photo is refused (409). Sharing never grants marketing or publication use (HH-PRIV-02). Audited with who and when.

post.summary: Stop sharing a field photo with the customer
post.description: Owner or Office (media.share_with_customer), with the version they saw (PROPOSED). Makes a shared field photo internal again: the customer no longer reaches it by the tab, its ID or a new link (a link already issued expires within minutes). Audited with who and when.

post.summary: Record a customer’s permission to publish a field photo, or its withdrawal
post.description: The Owner (media.mark_marketing_eligible: marketing use needs recorded consent). Records, for one ready field photo, the evidenced permission of the customer of its project to publish it for the purpose and channel (PROPOSED: marketing on the website), under the configured publication notice version (media.publication_notice; NOT CONFIGURED: 503 NOT_CONFIGURED, nothing recorded; another version: 400), with how the customer gave it and a staff reference to the evidence. granted false records the customer’s withdrawal: new use stops at once. Append-only: the latest record per photo, purpose and channel is current. Sharing with the customer never creates one, and this never shares the photo. A restricted or unready photo: 409.

post.summary: Cancel a hold entered in error
post.description: The Owner (job_hold.set_ready, PROPOSED). Only for a hold entered in error, with the reason; the hold and its reason stay in the history.

The Owner (job_hold.set_ready, PROPOSED for review holds; OWN-DEC-137). Needs a note saying how it was resolved and who reviewed it (name and, where the hazard needs one, their qualification). No checkbox, timer, acknowledgment or AI output clears a hold. Nobody resolves a critical safety hold they raised.
Staff with job_hold.set (PROPOSED). Moves an open review hold to "under review"; it still blocks the estimate path. If-Match is the hold version.

get.description: Staff with message.reply, inside the caller’s project scope (Owner, Office: every project; an Estimator’s own threads are not recorded yet, so none). Customer conversations, latest activity first, each with its project, customer, whether a customer reply waits and a short preview of the latest message. Internal conversations and Needs Linking messages are never listed here.

Staff with message.reply on the conversation’s project, inside the caller’s scope (an unknown or out-of-scope ID is NOT_FOUND). The customer conversation’s inbound email and texts as received (the original text, never changed; attachments as metadata only, not imported), each with its sender contact or "unknown sender"; the project’s customer notifications as delivery metadata (no text); and, kept apart, the project’s internal conversation, which never reaches the customer.

post.description: Staff with message.reply on the conversation’s project, inside the caller’s scope. Records who handled the customer’s replies and when, and resolves the conversation’s "customer replied" queue item. Nothing is sent and no message changes.

get.summary: An inbound message and its linking
get.description: Owner and Office only (message.view_unmatched). One inbound email or text exactly as received, its linking state (matched, Needs Linking with the reason, or linked by staff), its linking history with each correction’s staff member and reason, and candidate projects: projects of customers whose contacts have the sender’s exact address (marked when the address is verified) and the project a reference suggested. Candidates are suggestions for staff, never links.

post.summary: Link a message to a project, or return it to Needs Linking
post.description: Owner and Office only (message.link), with If-Match (the message’s linking version) and a written reason. Links an inbound message to the project with that reference (any project inside the caller’s scope), or, with projectReference null, returns it to Needs Linking. The message itself never changes: only its linking moves, and the correction is kept in its linking history and the audit log (OWN-DEC-120). The sender is recorded as a contact of the project’s customer only when one of that customer’s contacts already has the exact address; no contact is created and nothing is merged.

get.description: Owner and Office only (message.view_unmatched); every other role is refused. Inbound email and texts that no reliable reference placed on exactly one project (several possible projects, none, a shared contact, or a reference whose sender is not on the project), newest first, with the reason and, when a reference named a project, that project as a suggestion. Nothing here is attached to any customer until staff link it.

get.summary: The customer conversation of a project
get.description: Staff with message.reply on the project, inside the caller’s scope (otherwise NOT_FOUND). The project, its customer and the id of its customer conversation, or null while no message has been received or sent yet: the reply composer of the project starts it with the first reply. Nothing is created by this read.

post.summary: Add an internal message to a project
post.description: Staff with message.reply on the project, inside the caller’s scope. Adds a staff-only message to the project’s internal conversation, which is separate from the customer conversation and never reaches the customer (HH-COM-01). A message never becomes a binding scope or price change. Card numbers are refused; never write passwords or access codes in a message.

post.summary: Send a reply to the customer from the project
post.description: Staff with message.reply on the project, inside the caller’s scope (otherwise NOT_FOUND). Pressing Send is the release; there is no second approval (OWN-DEC-120). The reply is added to the project’s customer conversation exactly as written (the customer reads it in the portal’s Messages tab) and its one email or text is released through the chosen channel: the preferred channel while it is permitted, otherwise one of the permitted channels staff chose (CONFLICT PREFERRED_CHANNEL_AVAILABLE, CHANNEL_UNAVAILABLE or NO_PERMITTED_CHANNEL otherwise; never switched silently). An email goes at once, at any hour; a text inside the recipient’s permitted hours, otherwise at their next opening (messages.delivery_hours). The consent, the contact and the English template are rechecked at send time; the delivery records what truly happened, and a failure becomes a delivery issue with Retry. With the same Idempotency-Key a retried submission returns the first answer and sends nothing more. Card numbers are refused; never write passwords or access codes in a reply. The audit event records the project, channel and send time, never the text.

get.summary: How a reply on this project can be sent
get.description: Staff with message.reply on the project, inside the caller’s scope (otherwise NOT_FOUND). The contact a reply goes to (the contact of the project’s request), the customer’s preferred channel, and for email and text whether each is permitted now (email: the address verified and service messages not withdrawn; text: the number verified and a current SMS opt-in, which a STOP withdraws), the channel Send uses without a choice (the preferred one while it is permitted; null: staff choose among the permitted ones, never switched silently), when a reply sent now goes out by each channel (TSK-0122: the email at once, at any hour; the text inside the recipient’s permitted hours, 8 AM–10 PM in their verified zone or 9 AM–9 PM Eastern while it is unknown, otherwise at their next opening), whether released reply wording exists per channel, and the longest reply.

Staff with message.reply. Whether each inbound channel is configured (Bird texts, Resend email: their webhook signing secrets), whether email bodies can be read and whether reply tokens are configured, by state only: never a secret, an address or a value. While a secret is unset the channel is "Inbound not configured" and nothing is shown as received. Also the count of inbound events on unsupported channels, and, for holders of message.view_unmatched only, how many messages wait in Needs Linking.

post.summary: Invite a staff member with a role
post.description: Owner only, with fresh authentication (ROLE-MATRIX staff.invite). Creates an invited account with no password and its role grant, and emails a single-use invite link through the outbox. There is no public registration.

Staff with invoice.issue (the Owner, Office; OWN-DEC-138). With If-Match: the invoice version shown. A final invoice is issued only once the Owner’s quality review lets it be (finance.invoice_quality_gate: CONFLICT QUALITY_REVIEW_NOT_RECORDED, QUALITY_REVIEW_BLOCKED or QUALITY_REVIEW_OWNER_ONLY), from the job’s current approved scope (SCOPE_CHANGED otherwise), with no deposit check pending (DEPOSIT_CHECK_PENDING); the deposit’s verified money is credited once. A deposit invoice is issued while its deposit is still due. The issuer name NOT CONFIGURED is NOT_CONFIGURED; the missing mailing address and placeholder contact and payment details block nothing. Pins the number (project reference and -I<n>), issuer, contact and payment instructions; the invoice never changes afterwards. Writes invoice.issued or invoice.deposit_issued: the PDF and the one customer notice follow. Returns the job’s invoices.

post.summary: Record a verified payment on an issued invoice
post.description: Staff with payment.record (the Owner, Office; a Worker only for their own on-site collection with the collect capability on an assigned job). After staff verified the payment: method (one of payment.methods), amount in cents, the date received (not after today), the collector (default: the caller), the transaction reference (required for Square card payments and checks) and the payer for a check; the same method and reference are refused twice. Applied, under the invoice’s lock, to what the invoice still asks for counting pending checks; an overpayment’s remainder stays unallocated for the Owner’s credit or refund decision (Owner Decisions), never a negative balance. A check is pending until the Owner clears it. Paid exactly when confirmed payments and credits reach the total (invoice.paid, once). A deposit invoice is paid through the deposit (CONFLICT). Returns the job’s invoices.

The Owner only. Dismisses the work-paused notice draft of this report: kept as cancelled (dismissed), never sent. The customer portal still shows "Work is paused for safety review." while the hold blocks.

The Owner only (message.release_draft, and the notice is Owner-released: OWN-DEC-152 section 3.2). Sends the owner-worded work_paused notice of this report to the customer through the send job, which checks the report's hold again at send time (released or cancelled by then: not sent). A notice that is not a draft is CONFLICT NOTICE_NOT_DRAFT. It carries no technical or incident detail.

post.summary: Add a photo to a report (only when safe)
post.description: Staff with job.add_photo (the Owner and workers assigned to the report's job); on a restricted report only the Owner and its reporter. Raw JPEG, PNG or WebP bytes, checked like request photos (content, type, size; NOT CONFIGURED limits or storage answer UNAVAILABLE), stored once under an opaque key in the private bucket with the report's visibility: never shared with the customer, never in a gallery or worker-wide feed. Photos are taken only when it is safe to do so; a report never needs one. If anything is unsafe: stop the affected work, keep people away and call the Owner; in an emergency call 911 at once, without waiting for anyone.

post.summary: The Owner's review of an issue report
post.description: Staff with issue_report.review (the Owner; PROPOSED cell in the case-closure row). Records once that the Owner reviewed a non-critical issue report (with an optional note) and resolves its field_issue queue item with the job's last one. A critical report is reviewed through its hold's documented release path, never here (CONFLICT REVIEWED_THROUGH_HOLD); a second review is CONFLICT ALREADY_REVIEWED.

Staff with job.report_issue (the Owner and workers assigned to the report's job); on a restricted report only the Owner and its reporter. Only on a Stop Work (a report with a critical hold; else CONFLICT NOT_A_STOP). Recorded separately from change orders: the trigger, the actions taken, why they were necessary, evidence, when the Owner and the customer were told, and the follow-up; it updates the hold's safety queue item for the Owner. The app lists no make-safe steps: none is approved in an SOP yet (NOT CONFIGURED until competent review). Gas and potentially live wiring are never handled; this never releases or weakens the hold.

post.summary: Set Ready on a job-level Hold / Ready note
post.description: Staff with job_hold.set_ready (the Owner), with the version they saw. Sets Ready on any job-level Hold / Ready note, including one the Owner set (OWN-DEC-137), with a note recording how the requirement was resolved; the Owner is recorded as the reviewer. Never a critical safety hold, a review hold or a task block (NOT_FOUND here): those have their own documented paths.

get.description: Staff with job.view_packet on the job. The approved total (the job’s latest scope snapshot) and the money paid, apart from every change order: its number, origin, current version (state, reason, proposed scope, schedule impact, hazards, resources, evidence, the checklist steps that wait for it, lines and totals) and earlier versions, with what the caller may do. A draft or reviewed change binds nothing (HH-CHG-02). Also the work packages with their checklist steps and the job’s field photos, to name in a draft.

post.summary: Propose or draft a change order
post.description: Staff with change_order.draft on the job (an assigned worker, an Estimator, the Owner), while the job is between its approval and operationally complete (JOB_NOT_OPEN_FOR_CHANGES otherwise). A new change order, numbered per project (<reference>-C<n>), with its first version as a draft: reason, proposed scope, charge and credit lines (credits are positive amounts that lower the total, OWN-DEC-203), schedule impact, hazards, resources, evidence photos and measurements, and the checklist steps that wait for it. A worker’s draft is always a worker proposal; an Estimator or the Owner names the origin. It binds nothing: the scope, the packet and every total stay as approved.

get.description: Staff with job.record_checklist_step: assigned to the job inside the access window. Per work package, the pinned SOP version in six ordered stages with every step verbatim, whether it is required, the evidence it asks for and the controls quoted before it; each step’s state, evidence, skip reason, worker and the actions the caller may take now; the current stage and the summary (required steps open or skipped). Also the job’s field photos to attach as evidence, the handoff notes, and what blocks the caller (JOB_NOT_IN_PROGRESS, HOLD_OPEN, WORK_NOT_STARTED).

post.description: Staff with job.record_checklist_step, after their own Start Work on the job: a note for whoever continues (optionally a named worker and a work package). The steps keep their state and history; the next worker continues where the checklist stopped.

Staff with job.record_checklist_step, after their own Start Work on the job, while the job and the work package are in progress and no hold is open. The step (workPackageId, stepId) at the version shown (0 when not started): not started or in progress -> completed, with every evidence the step asks for: photoIds (field photos of this job and work package), a measurement, a note (EVIDENCE_MISSING otherwise). Recorded with the caller as its worker; the history keeps every change.

Staff with job.record_checklist_step, after their own Start Work on the job, while the job and the work package are in progress and no hold is open. The step (workPackageId, stepId) at the version shown (0 when not started): in progress -> paused; the progress stays. Recorded with the caller as its worker; the history keeps every change.

Staff with job.record_checklist_step, after their own Start Work on the job, while the job and the work package are in progress and no hold is open. The step (workPackageId, stepId) at the version shown (0 when not started): completed or skipped -> in progress, with a reason; the earlier evidence is kept. Recorded with the caller as its worker; the history keeps every change.

Staff with job.record_checklist_step, after their own Start Work on the job, while the job and the work package are in progress and no hold is open. The step (workPackageId, stepId) at the version shown (0 when not started): paused -> in progress. Recorded with the caller as its worker; the history keeps every change.

Staff with job.record_checklist_step, after their own Start Work on the job, while the job and the work package are in progress and no hold is open. The step (workPackageId, stepId) at the version shown (0 when not started): not started, in progress or paused -> skipped, with a reason; a skipped required step blocks completion. Recorded with the caller as its worker; the history keeps every change.

Staff with job.record_checklist_step, after their own Start Work on the job, while the job and the work package are in progress and no hold is open. The step (workPackageId, stepId) at the version shown (0 when not started): not started -> in progress, once every step of the earlier stages is completed or skipped. Recorded with the caller as its worker; the history keeps every change.

get.summary: What Finished needs for a job
get.description: Staff with job.record_walkthrough: assigned to the job inside the access window. Per work package, whether its checklist is complete and how many before and after photos it has; every problem that blocks Finished (CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE, BEFORE_PHOTO_MISSING, AFTER_PHOTO_MISSING per package; JOB_NOT_IN_PROGRESS, HOLD_OPEN, WORK_NOT_STARTED, ALREADY_SUBMITTED); and, once submitted, the walkthrough and who submitted it when.

post.summary: Record the walkthrough and submit the job for quality review
post.description: Staff with job.record_walkthrough, after their own Start Work on the job. The walkthrough outcome: accepted ("Everything looks good"), accepted_with_follow_up, disputed ("I have a concern") or customer_unavailable; the participant and their standing for every outcome but customer_unavailable (which names nobody and is never acceptance); comments, required for a concern or follow-up items. A concern opens a dispute case for the Owner. Then Finished: the job becomes ready_for_qa ("Awaiting quality review", never complete), its work packages complete, and the Owner’s quality review opens. Refused (CONFLICT, every problem named) unless every work package’s checklist is complete and has before and after photos, no hold is open, the job is in progress and not already submitted.

get.summary: A job's deposit requirement, its payments and the waiver
get.description: Staff with payment.view (the Owner, Office). The deposit the approval pinned (required with its amount in cents, or not required; the rule version and the approved total after any discount it was computed on), its state, the verified and pending (uncleared check) amounts applied, what it still needs, whether work visits may be confirmed as it stands, the Square payment link of the deposit request, the waiver with its reason, every payment recorded on the job and the actions the server would allow the caller now.

put.summary: Enter the deposit request's Square payment link
put.description: Staff with invoice.enter_payment_link (the Owner, Office; OWN-DEC-138). With If-Match: the deposit version shown. The deposit-specific link staff created in the Square app: https on a host of payment.square_link_hosts (PROPOSED list; NOT CONFIGURED refuses). Only while the deposit is still due. Nothing is charged here and nothing returns from Square: a redirect or a customer claim never marks the deposit paid. Returns the deposit view.

post.description: Staff with payment.record (the Owner, Office; a Worker only for their own on-site collection with the collect capability on an assigned job). After staff verified the payment: method (one of payment.methods), amount in cents, the date received (not after today), the collector (default: the caller), the transaction reference (required for Square card payments and checks) and the payer for a check. The same method and reference are refused twice (CONFLICT DUPLICATE_PAYMENT). Applied, under the deposit lock, to what the deposit still needs; a remainder stays unapplied for the Owner. A check is received and pending: it satisfies nothing until cleared. Returns the deposit view.

post.summary: Waive this job's required deposit (Owner only)
post.description: The Owner only (deposit.waive; OWN-DEC-76): a fresh sign-in (password or authenticator code within 5 minutes, read again at the write) and a written reason. Every other role, including another administrator, is refused. Job-specific; only while the deposit is still due. It never marks the deposit paid and never changes the price; work visits of the job may then be confirmed. Append-only and audited. Returns the deposit view.

Staff with hazard.report: every worker assigned to the job ("A, always, no permission needed"), Office, the Estimator and the Owner. No fresh sign-in, reason, version or rate limit: nothing stands in front of it, and nothing about the job's state refuses it (other holds, a failing Start Work gate, a paused job, an old packet). One transaction under the job lock: a critical safety hold (written first, naming the report), the job moved from in_progress to paused, the affected work packages blocked (the named ones; the whole job for a gas leak, live wiring, hazardous material, a structural concern or an injury), the report itself and a top-priority safety queue item. Every field is optional: the hazard defaults to other_unsafe, a long text is cut, an id the server cannot place is left out. An injury's details are restricted to the Owner and the reporter. The answer carries the guidance to show at once (a gas leak: evacuate and call from a safe place; live wiring: never touched), the reviewer the hazard needs (named, never decided), resolveOnSite false and Call 911. The work-paused customer notice is drafted for the Owner to release (never automatic); the customer portal shows only "Work is paused for safety review." Releasing the hold is the documented path of /staff/critical-holds (never by the person who raised it). The same Idempotency-Key from an offline phone records it once.

get.summary: The caller's own incident reports on a job
get.description: Staff with incident.report on the job (an assigned worker, the Owner, Office, an Estimator). Only the reports the caller made: number, kind, type, state and when; never anyone else’s report.

post.summary: Report an incident from the job screen
post.description: Staff with incident.report: a worker assigned to the job (inside the access window), the Owner, Office or an Estimator. Quick, from the job screen; linked to the job and its project. An incident, property damage, injury or dispute is recorded factually and minimally: what happened, the people affected, work areas, immediate actions and only the medical detail that is necessary, all in the restricted section (readable by the Owner and the person who reported it only, OWN-DEC-143). The type sets the kind: injury, damage (property_damage), dispute, or incident for the others. Damage, injury and disputes notify the Owner at once: an Owner Decisions item and a staff notification (case.opened). The responsible reviewer is the Owner. A safety hazard needs Stop Work / Report Hazard, not this report: nothing here raises or clears a hold.

get.summary: A job's invoices, their money and what blocks issuing
get.description: Staff with payment.view (the Owner, Office). The job’s final and deposit invoices: lines in integer cents (charges, and credit lines as positive magnitudes), the discount row, the total, the deposit credit (pinned at issue; for a draft, what the deposit’s verified money would credit now), and once issued the number, issuer, money (invoiced, credits, confirmed paid, pending checks, remaining) and the payments applied. A draft lists its exceptions; blocking ones refuse the issue (the Owner’s quality review, TSK-0084: QUALITY_REVIEW_NOT_RECORDED until decided, QUALITY_REVIEW_BLOCKED while a major punch item is open). Also the job’s unallocated money (for the Owner’s decision) and the actions the server would allow the caller now.

post.description: Staff with invoice.issue (the Owner, Office). Prepares the deposit invoice draft of a job whose required deposit is still due: one line, the deposit amount the approval pinned. A job without a required deposit, or whose deposit is paid, waived or applied, is a CONFLICT. Returns the job’s invoices.

Staff with invoice.issue (the Owner, Office). Prepares the job’s final invoice draft from its current approved scope (the latest job scope snapshot: the approved estimate lines and selected options, later the approved change orders) with the approved discount as its own totals row; brings an existing draft up to date (the approval already prepared one automatically). Never prices anything: a scope whose lines do not add up to its approved totals, or whose credits reach its charges, is a CONFLICT naming why. An issued final invoice is a CONFLICT (one per job). Returns the job’s invoices.

get.summary: A job's Stop Work, hazard and issue reports
get.description: Staff with work.stop (the assigned workers of the job, Office, the Estimator, the Owner). Every report of the job, newest first, with its severity, whether it paused the job and where its hold stands. A restricted report's details (an injury or an incident: what was reported, the text, the resolution, photos, stabilization, the reporter) are shown only to the Owner (audited) and the worker who reported it; everyone else sees that it exists and its status (OWN-DEC-143). The Owner also sees the work-paused customer notice drafts and may release or dismiss them. Lists the job's work packages for the forms and always carries Call 911. What the caller may do next: report a hazard, report an issue, add a photo, record stabilization, review.

post.description: Staff with job.report_issue (the Owner and workers assigned to the job). One of the issue categories of HH-WORK-08 with its severity, description, the affected work package and the next owner. A critical issue or an unsafe condition takes the Stop Work path (critical hold, pause, queue item in the same transaction). An on-site resolution (what happened, the steps, the materials, how the result was checked, and the worker's statement that the fix is within their training, qualifications, the approved scope and the approved SOP) is refused with CONFLICT for a critical issue, an unsafe condition or an incident (RESOLVE_ON_SITE_NOT_OFFERED) and while a critical safety hold of the job is unresolved (SAFETY_HOLD_OPEN). Every non-critical report notifies the Owner (field_issue queue item). An incident is restricted to the Owner and the reporter; its case record is TSK-0093, and a customer change becomes a change-order draft with TSK-0082. If anything is unsafe: stop the affected work, keep people away and call the Owner; in an emergency call 911 at once, without waiting for anyone.

post.summary: Set the job-level Hold with a note
post.description: Staff with job_hold.set (the Owner; Office and the Estimator, PROPOSED cells). Puts the job on Hold with a note naming the unresolved requirement (OWN-DEC-82: no license or credential module; licenses and permits are checked by the Owner outside the software) and its category. Written under the job lock: while it blocks, the job's visits cannot be confirmed and work cannot start. Only the Owner sets Ready, with a note. The packet gets a new version (a critical change: every assigned worker reviews it again).

get.summary: A job's loadout: what to load per work package, what was stated, and what blocks
get.description: Staff with job.view_packet inside their scope (as for the job packet: the Owner and Office; the Estimator (PROPOSED cell); a worker only while assigned to a live visit of the job). The server first brings the packet up to date, which pins each package's loadout version once. For each work package: the list as the vault inventory file writes it (its groups, items with their vault line, review notes and the proposed additions, which are not approved and never items), PROPOSED every item required; each item's latest statement (loaded, missing, damaged, or an approved substitute) with who and when; the readiness Start Work reads (ready, not confirmed, blocked, or NOT CONFIGURED when the service has no list); and the task blocks with their owner, action and what the caller may do. No quantity is ever added.

post.summary: State what is loaded, missing or damaged
post.description: Staff with job.record_loadout (PROPOSED in the field-records row: the Owner and workers, assigned jobs only, inside the access window). For one work package of the job, states per item: loaded (loaded and available), missing or damaged, with an optional note. A missing or damaged required item raises a task block on that work package in the same transaction, under the job lock (one per item while it blocks), with its owner and action (the Owner provides the item or approves a substitute), and the packet gets a new version. Start Work stays blocked for that package only. A later "loaded" is recorded but releases nothing: only the Owner's recorded resolution does. Each item once per call; only items of the pinned list. Audited (counts only).

get.description: Staff with job.view_packet inside their scope: the Owner and Office; the Estimator (PROPOSED cell); a worker only while assigned to a live visit of the job (an active confirmed reservation, until the end of the service day; a removed worker is refused on the next request). The server first brings the packet up to date (a new version when its records changed). Answers the version, its first-generated, last-updated and checked times, whether it is the latest, "What changed since you reviewed this?" against the version the caller last viewed, and every section of HH-PKT-01 from stored records only (no price, never an access code: a code is revealed separately, online, on the visit date). What no record holds is marked, never filled in. Also where the caller's own acknowledgment stands (acknowledged, required, invalidated by a critical change, a removed assignment or a disabled account, or not assigned) with what changed since the acknowledged version, and each assigned worker's state. Nobody inherits another person's acknowledgment.

post.summary: Record the caller's own acknowledgment of the latest packet version
post.description: Staff with job.view_packet who are themselves assigned to the job right now (an active confirmed reservation on a live visit, inside its access window; PROPOSED: the matrix has no acknowledgment row). Records that the caller personally reviewed the given version: it must be the latest one with the exact content digest the caller read (else CONFLICT PACKET_CHANGED: review the new version). Personal: nobody acknowledges for another person and nobody inherits one (CONFLICT NOT_ASSIGNED for anyone not assigned). Acknowledging the standing version again adds nothing (200). Also records the view of that version. A critical change, the end of the caller's assignment or a disabled account later ends it, once. It never releases a hold and is not the Start Job gate by itself. Audited.

post.summary: Record a print of a packet version
post.description: Staff with job.view_packet inside their scope (as for the packet; PROPOSED: printing uses the view permission). Records and audits the print of the given version (who, when, which version, the latest version then); the staff app then prints its print view, which carries the version and "Printed <time>; check the app for changes" and never an access code. An older version is recorded as stale.

get.summary: The printable PDF of a packet version
get.description: Staff with job.view_packet inside their scope (as for the packet). The PDF of the given version (default: the latest), in the caller's interface language: every page says "Printed <time>; check the app for changes" with the version, an older version says it is not the latest, and it never contains an access code, a code label, a price or a photo link. Each download is recorded and audited as an export (who, when, which version). Never cached. PROPOSED limit: 60 per staff member per hour.

get.summary: The versions of a job packet
get.description: Staff with job.view_packet inside their scope (as for the packet). Every version, newest first, with when it was generated, what changed against the version before it and whether a change was critical (scope, holds, SOP version, assignment, site access). Versions are never changed or deleted.

post.summary: Record that the caller viewed a packet version
post.description: Staff with job.view_packet inside their scope (as for the packet). Records that the caller viewed the given version (a version the job has), so the packet later shows what changed since then. Personal: it records the caller only. A view is not an acknowledgment: it releases nothing and passes no gate. Audited.

get.summary: The field photos of a job
get.description: Staff who view the job packet (job.view_packet: Owner, Office, the assigned Worker inside the access window). Every before and after photo of the job by work package, with its visit, area label, pair, processing state (quarantined, ready, rejected), visibility class, who uploaded it and when, and for a ready one a signed URL valid for minutes. A restricted photo is listed only for a role that reads its class. Per photo: the current publication permission per channel and the actions the caller may take (share, stop sharing: media.share_with_customer; record a publication permission: media.mark_marketing_eligible). Also the visits where the caller may upload now (assigned and arrived; after photos once their own work start is recorded) and the configured publication notice version (null while NOT CONFIGURED). An Estimator reads estimating scope only: FORBIDDEN here.

get.summary: The caller's punch items on a job
get.description: Staff with quality.correct_punch_item on the job (a worker assigned to it, inside the access window). Only the punch items assigned to the caller, with what to correct, the required evidence and the due date.

Staff with quality.review (the Owner). What the Owner reviews (HH-QA-02): the approved scope lines, the work packages, the before/after photo counts, whether a checklist and a walkthrough are recorded (TSK-0075, TSK-0083), the open critical safety holds of the job; the review (state, reviewer, self-review, the area results), the final-invoice gate it gives, every punch item with its correction and re-check, the history, the workers an item may be assigned to and the actions the caller may take.

post.description: Staff with quality.review (the Owner), with If-Match (the review version), on a review in review: a result (ok or problem) for the scope, the checklist, the before/after evidence and the walkthrough, and an optional note. With no punch item and every area ok the review passes and the job becomes operationally complete (HH-QA-09); with punch items it asks for punch work (the final invoice then follows the items: blocked while a major one is not re-checked, the Owner only while only minor ones remain). A problem with no punch item is refused (PROBLEM_NEEDS_PUNCH_ITEM): every problem becomes a punch item.

post.summary: Start the quality review of a job
post.description: Staff with quality.review (the Owner), on a job awaiting quality review (CONFLICT JOB_NOT_AWAITING_REVIEW otherwise): pending -> in_review with the caller as the reviewer. Marked self-review when the reviewer started work on the job (OWN-DEC-64). Once only (REVIEW_ALREADY_STARTED).

Staff with quality.manage_punch_items (the Owner), while the review is in review, asks for punch work or waits for re-check (a new item then sends it back to punch work). The problem, its kind (finish or cleanup: minor; defect, incomplete scope, failed check or safety concern: major, OWN-DEC-64), the work package of the job or a named area, the required correction evidence, an active worker to correct it and a due date. A safety concern names the job's open critical safety hold (report it first through Stop Work / Report Hazard: SAFETY_HOLD_REQUIRED). Opens the punch-items queue item.

get.summary: A job's holds and Start Work exceptions
get.description: Staff with job_hold.set (the Owner; Office and the Estimator, PROPOSED cells). The holds of the job that block Start Work (job-level Hold / Ready notes, critical safety holds, intake review holds) open or under review, and the ones resolved or cancelled, with the actions the caller may take: the Owner sets Ready on any job-level note (including one the Owner set) and reviews, resolves or cancels a critical safety hold they did not raise. For the Owner (work.approve_exception) also every exception of the job with its reason, evidence, where it stands, its follow-up (a pending upload or reconciliation stays open until resolved) and the Owner's actions; nobody else sees exceptions here.

The Owner only (dashboard.view, and the Owner role checked again). The launch phase in force (launch.phase: owner_acceptance_testing, invited_customers or public; phase 1 when it cannot be read), the switches it sets (invited customers, public submissions, search indexing: all off in phase 1), what they mean in this environment (outside production nothing is public whatever the phase: testers only, never indexed), the moves the Owner may make with the words to type for each, and the history of phase decisions with who made them and the approval they recorded. ETag: the configuration version. Reads only.

put.summary: Move the launch phase (the Owner only)
put.description: The Owner only (policy_values.change: a fresh sign-in within 5 minutes, and the Owner role checked again), with If-Match: the configuration version shown, the words to type for this move (confirmation, from getLaunchPhase) and the Owner’s written approval (reason). Moves one step forward (phase 1 to 2 after the Owner approves Owner Acceptance Testing, 2 to 3 after the Owner approves the invited-customer launch) or back to any earlier phase; anything else is VALIDATION_FAILED (SAME_PHASE, SKIPS_A_PHASE, confirmation_mismatch) and changes nothing. Records the next launch.phase version citing OWN-DEC-191 with the approval as its reason, and an audit event with the old and new phase, in one transaction; the database refuses a change that is not the Owner’s, not recorded or not one allowed step. Refusals are audited too.

post.summary: Cancel a task block entered in error
post.description: The Owner (job_hold.set_ready). Only for a block entered in error, with the reason; the block, the worker's statement and the reason stay in the history. The item still needs a "loaded" statement before its package is ready.

post.summary: Resolve a task block under review
post.description: The Owner (job_hold.set_ready; PROPOSED for task blocks). With a note saying how it was resolved and who assessed it, either: item_provided (the item was stated loaded after the block was raised and is still loaded) or substitute_approved (the substitute named, never "equivalent", with what it affects: safety, appearance, specification, price, warranty). A substitute that affects the customer is a change order (HH-CHG-02), NOT CONFIGURED until change orders exist: refused with CHANGE_ORDER_REQUIRED. No checkbox, timer, acknowledgment or AI output clears a block.

Staff with job_hold.set (the Owner; Office and Estimator PROPOSED) inside their scope. Moves an open task block to "under review"; it still blocks Start Work on its work package. If-Match is the block version.

get.description: Owner only (staff.view; PROPOSED in the staff-management row). Every staff account, disabled ones too (their history is kept): name, login email, locale, status and its times, live roles and capabilities, whether a password is set and an authenticator enrolled, live sessions, and how many upcoming assignments the person has and how many are flagged for review. Never a hash, token or link.

Owner only (staff.view). The member with every role and capability grant (live and ended, who issued and ended it, the reason), the disabling and re-enabling history, and the upcoming assignments (reservations of visits) with their review flags.

post.description: Owner only (staff.disable; never delayed). In one transaction, after the in-flight writes of the person commit: the account is disabled (every later request and every queued or offline write from it is refused), every session is revoked, every open invite or reset link invalidated, the password cleared (PROPOSED) and the authenticator with its recovery codes removed (OWN-DEC-202: a re-enabled account enrols again); the upcoming assignments are flagged for reassignment and each flagged visit opens its action-queue item, never cancelled; job history and evidence stay. Refusals: NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (ACCOUNT_DISABLED, LAST_OWNER, OWN_ACCOUNT, PROPOSED).

Owner only, with a fresh sign-in and a written reason (staff.enable, PROPOSED in the grant row; ENT-StaffUser). The account returns to active (invited when it never set a password) with its role grants unchanged, and a single-use reset (or invite) link is emailed through the outbox: the old password was cleared when it was disabled. Refusals: NOT_FOUND, FRESH_AUTH_REQUIRED, FORBIDDEN (self), CONFLICT (ACCOUNT_NOT_DISABLED).

Owner only, with a fresh sign-in and a written reason (ROLE-MATRIX staff.grant_role); nobody grants themselves anything. Roles: owner, office, estimator, worker (one person may hold several); capability: collect, only for someone holding the Worker role (PROPOSED). Takes effect on the next request of that person. Refusals: NOT_FOUND, FRESH_AUTH_REQUIRED, FORBIDDEN (self), CONFLICT (ACCOUNT_DISABLED, GRANT_EXISTS, CAPABILITY_NEEDS_WORKER), VALIDATION_FAILED.

post.summary: End a role or capability grant
post.description: Owner only (staff.end_grant; protective, never delayed by a fresh sign-in, PROPOSED mapping; ENT-RoleGrant). The grant is ended, never edited or deleted; the reason, when given, is audited. PROPOSED: the person keeps at least one role (disable the account instead). At least one active Owner always remains. Refusals: NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (GRANT_NOT_LIVE, LAST_ROLE, LAST_OWNER).

post.summary: Reset a staff member's lost authenticator
post.description: Owner only, with a fresh sign-in and a written reason, never for oneself (staff.reset_mfa, PROPOSED in the grant row; TSK-0154, OWN-DEC-202). Removes the authenticator and its recovery codes and revokes every session of the person at once; their next sign-in (with their password) enrols a new authenticator before any staff screen. MFA stays mandatory: nothing turns it off. An Owner's own lost authenticator: a recovery code, or the operations command reset-mfa (PROPOSED). Refusals: NOT_FOUND, FRESH_AUTH_REQUIRED, FORBIDDEN (self), VALIDATION_FAILED (reason), CONFLICT (ACCOUNT_DISABLED, MFA_NOT_ENROLLED).

post.summary: Start password recovery for a staff member
post.description: Owner only (staff.start_password_recovery; never delayed). Emails a single-use reset link (an invite link while the account is invited) through the outbox; earlier open links end. Setting the new password revokes every session. The Owner never sees a password or the link. Refusals: NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (ACCOUNT_DISABLED).

get.summary: Outgoing messages and their delivery state
get.description: Staff with message.release_draft, inside the caller’s project scope (Owner, Office: every message; others only what their scope reaches). Newest first. Each message shows its lifecycle state (DRAFT, PENDING_APPROVAL, SCHEDULED, QUEUED, PROVIDER_ACCEPTED, DELIVERED, FAILED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED, SUPPRESSED), template ID and version, channel, a masked destination, its created, queued, due, provider-accepted and status times, attempts and their history, the failure reason with the names of missing variables, the consent decision, whether a test provider intercepted it (never delivered) and whether its Retry is available. Filters: group (waiting, sent, failed, stopped) and reference (a project reference). Never the text, a value or a full destination.

post.description: The Retry action of a delivery_failed queue item (HH-INT-20, HH-COM-02). Queues a failed delivery of an automatic message again, only when it never reached the provider: a new job of the message’s own automation sends it, rechecking the automatic list, the template, consent and the record, under the same provider idempotency key, so a retry sends at most one message. A failed staff reply (TSK-0050) is released again the same way, and so is a failed estimate, question or appointment reminder (TSK-0121): an email at once, a text at the next allowed time of the recipient’s permitted hours (TSK-0122). A delivery that is not failed (queued, sent, suppressed), any other staff-released draft, a message no longer on the automatic list or a delivery without an open delivery issue is a CONFLICT; so is an uncertain provider outcome (fieldErrors code OUTCOME_UNKNOWN), which is reconciled against the provider instead (HH-ARC-09). A re-run that sends nothing leaves the delivery failed with its reason. Staff with message.release_draft; an Estimator only for deliveries of records they are responsible for. The queue item resolves once the send is handed over.

get.summary: Message templates and the variable registry
get.description: Staff with message.release_draft. Every message type with its owner template ID, audience, channels, classification and release authority (automatic while on messages.automatic, staff-released, or released by the Owner), and per channel and language its newest released version (append-only) and readiness: ready, NOT CONFIGURED (no approved wording) or not wired (the values its wording needs are not supplied yet). Also the one template-variable registry: each variable’s kind, meaning, source record, whether it may appear in a subject, whether it is required (only a variable with an approved fallback is optional) and whether it is sensitive. Template approval is shown separately from any message’s delivery state.

get.summary: Preview a released template with sample values
get.description: Staff with message.release_draft. The newest released version of one message type for a channel and language (customer messages are English), rendered through the same branded layout as a real send with synthetic sample values on the reserved example.test host: subject, plain text and HTML. A preview is never sent or recorded as a delivery. NOT_FOUND for an unknown type, a channel it does not use, or no released version (NOT CONFIGURED).

get.summary: The HTML preview page of a released email template
get.description: As previewMessageTemplate, for email: the rendered HTML itself, for a sandboxed frame in the staff app. Served with its own policy (sandbox, no scripts, no requests, inline styles only, framed only by the same origin). NOT_FOUND for a text-message channel or no released version.

Staff with schedule.view_my_day: only the caller's own active reservations (a worker's own assignments; a tentative hold shows no address and no actions). Lists the visits of today in each visit's zone, and any visit still on the way or arrived, in arrival-window order: the window, the address and a plain directions link (confirmed and live, on the visit's own local service day only, OWN-DEC-171), the access notes (never a code), the preparation, the readiness blockers the records show (blocking holds, a deposit not yet covered, a work package without an SOP, a packet not viewed or changed since, the caller's own packet acknowledgment missing or ended, a loadout task block, required loadout items not confirmed or a loadout NOT CONFIGURED; this is not the Start Work check and never refuses a tap), the caller's own taps and the one next action. No ETA anywhere.

get.summary: The caller's assigned jobs and their packets
get.description: Staff with schedule.view_my_day: only the caller's own assignments (active confirmed reservations on live work visits whose service day has not ended), grouped by job, with the packet's current version (brought up to date first), the version the caller last viewed and whether it changed since then, critically or not, and where the caller's own acknowledgment stands. Nothing about another person's assignments.

post.description: The Owner only (check.mark_cleared; OWN-DEC-138), never for a check they collected. A received or deposited check becomes cleared; the deposit it was applied to counts it from now on. Any other payment or state is a CONFLICT. Returns the deposit view of the check's job.

get.description: Staff with payment.view (the Owner, Office). The Square payouts and fees recorded by hand, newest first (PAYOUT_LIST_LIMIT each): separate records, never part of a customer payment (HH-FIN-06).

post.description: Staff with payout.record (the Owner; Office PROPOSED). The Square payout ID, the net amount paid out in cents and the date (not after today). The same payout ID is refused twice. A payout never changes a customer balance: a verified payment counts when recorded (HH-FIN-06). Returns the payouts and fees.

get.description: Owner only (privacy.decide). Every privacy request in the order received, optionally of one state: the reference, kind, state, project, customer, the requesting contact, whether it came from a login account, and when it was received, reviewed and decided. Response deadlines are NOT CONFIGURED (OQ-PRIVACY-REQUESTS).

get.summary: One privacy request with its scoped search
get.description: Owner only (privacy.decide). The request, what the review found when it started, and the scoped search as it is now: every record kind held about the customer and the requester, counted, with what a deletion would do (delete, retain with the reason and until when where known, exclude third parties, none stored, not recorded), the hold checks and the checks the Owner must confirm (complaints, disputes, claims, invoices and payments are not recorded by the software yet), and what a confirmed deletion removes now.

post.summary: Complete or decline a privacy request
post.description: Owner only (privacy.decide), with a fresh sign-in and a written reason. Completing a deletion request deletes what the scoped search allows now (each estimate never accepted that nothing blocks, with its deletion log entry) and, with closeAccess, closes sign-in, sessions and project access links (OWN-DEC-71; allowed while a hold keeps records; an unpaid balance never blocks it); every not-recorded check must be listed in confirmedChecks (VALIDATION_FAILED CHECK_NOT_CONFIRMED). Everything else is retained, never cascaded into protected records; the outcome names the deleted and retained categories (partially_completed when anything is retained). Completing an export makes the export available to the requester; a correction records that it was handled in the records’ own screens. If-Match: the request version. Refusals: FRESH_AUTH_REQUIRED, CONFLICT REVIEW_NOT_STARTED / ALREADY_DECIDED / RECORD_CHANGED, STALE_VERSION, VALIDATION_FAILED.

post.summary: Open the review of a privacy request
post.description: Owner only (privacy.decide). received -> under_review, keeping what the scoped search found (categories and counts, never content). If-Match: the request version. Refusals: CONFLICT REVIEW_ALREADY_STARTED, STALE_VERSION.

get.description: Staff with case.view. Every case of the project, newest first, with the same projection as the case list: Office sees a restricted case only as that it exists and its status. The record screen offers "add to existing case" from the open complaints listed here.

post.description: Staff with case.record_complaint (the Owner, Office). A complaint from a walkthrough, a message or a call becomes a case linked to the project (and its job when given): category, severity, assigned person, due date and the description as staff wrote it (internal). An open complaint of the same category on the project refuses a second one (CONFLICT, body.category DUPLICATE_OPEN_CASE, with the open case in `current`), so staff add to the existing case instead. A damage claim, injury or dispute is reported as its own restricted case. Opens the case in the action queue; never stops any work and never contacts the customer.

get.description: Staff with estimate.draft. The estimates of one project with every version (state, total in integer cents), and whether the caller may Write an Estimate now (the project is open). The request record shows it.

post.description: Staff with estimate.draft, on an open project. Creates estimate <project reference>-E<n> with its first draft version, written in the staff app (HH-EST-11), copying the project payment term; the pending-estimate queue items of the project show the draft. No amount, price or message is created.

post.summary: Report an incident, damage, injury or dispute on a project
post.description: Staff with incident.report (the Owner, Office, Estimator; workers report from the job). An incident, property damage, injury or dispute is recorded factually and minimally: what happened, the people affected, work areas, immediate actions and only the medical detail that is necessary, all in the restricted section (readable by the Owner and the person who reported it only, OWN-DEC-143). The type sets the kind: injury, damage (property_damage), dispute, or incident for the others. Damage, injury and disputes notify the Owner at once: an Owner Decisions item and a staff notification (case.opened). The responsible reviewer is the Owner. A safety hazard needs Stop Work / Report Hazard, not this report: nothing here raises or clears a hold.

Staff with estimate.draft, on an open project. Creates estimate <project reference>-E<n> with its first draft version, authored by upload (HH-EST-11): the PDF or Word document is uploaded next, and the total, options, deposit and validity are the structured amounts saved with the draft. No amount is read from a document; no message is sent.

get.description: Staff with schedule.view_board (Owner, Office; Estimator PROPOSED). The visits of one project (estimate visits and the job's work visits), each with its purpose, state, version, current window (local date, arrival window, IANA zone, UTC offsets and instants, and whether it lies inside the daily visit hours of contact.hours in the business zone; null while NOT CONFIGURED) and every earlier window version. Beside them, kept apart, the project's job with its scope version and its scheduling task (never a booking), the property's zone, the business zone with its PROPOSED mark, and what the caller may plan now. Each tentative visit lists its confirmationBlockers (TSK-0064): every unmet confirmation precondition and missing visit fact, as field and code; Confirm is offered only when the list is empty (the team's capacity is checked on confirming). A timing preference on the request is never listed here.

post.description: Staff with visit.offer_windows: Owner and Office any purpose; an Estimator estimate visits only (PROPOSED). Creates one tentative visit: an Estimate visit (site_estimate) on an open project, with no job and no price approval, or a work visit (service, follow_up, return_work) on the project's job, which exists only after approval, after the job's scheduling gates pass. The window is a local date and arrival window in the property's IANA zone; a time inside a spring-forward gap is refused (LOCAL_TIME_GAP), a time inside a repeated hour needs its offset (LOCAL_TIME_REPEATED, then startOffset or endOffset such as "-05:00") and is stored with it, and a window must start in the future (WINDOW_IN_PAST, PROPOSED). NOT CONFIGURED while business.timezone is unset. PROPOSED: the first work visit moves the scheduling task to planning. Nothing is confirmed, reserved, shown to the customer or sent. Returns the project's visits.

get.description: Staff with customer.view, inside their scope (Owner, Office; Estimator PROPOSED; a worker reaches no property until visit assignments exist). The current address and its former addresses, the property type, each changeable detail with its source and last confirmation, the customers authorized for it, the requests made there with the address each was sent with (marked when it is a former address), and the change history. For roles that may enter or reveal access codes: the codes masked (kind, label, source, last confirmation, reveals), never their values, and whether the store is configured. The ETag is the property version.

post.description: Staff with access_code.set (Owner, Office). Stores a gate, lockbox, alarm or door code or a key location in the protected store, sealed; it is masked everywhere and opened only by the audited reveal. A label is a short non-secret name; a label or reason that repeats the code is refused. No idempotency key: the request hash would be a stored digest of the code. NOT_CONFIGURED while ACCESS_CODE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset.

put.summary: Replace an access code’s value
put.description: Staff with access_code.set (Owner, Office). Seals the new value in place of the old one, which is erased, with its source and the required reason (never repeating the code). If-Match is the code version; a removed code is not changed (ACCESS_CODE_REMOVED). No idempotency key (the body holds the code). NOT_CONFIGURED while ACCESS_CODE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset.

post.summary: Confirm an access code is still right
post.description: Staff with access_code.set (Owner, Office). Records that the code was confirmed unchanged now, with its source and the required reason; the value is neither read nor changed. If-Match is the code version.

Staff with access_code.set (Owner, Office). For a code no longer needed for authorized access (FACT-RETENTION-SCHEDULE): the sealed value is erased at once and the code can no longer be revealed; the record that it existed, who entered and who removed it, and the required reason are kept. Works while the store is NOT CONFIGURED. If-Match is the code version.

Staff with access_code.reveal: the Owner; Office (PROPOSED cell); a worker only when assigned to a visit at the property (an active confirmed reservation on a live visit there, TSK-0069), on the visit date (business time zone), online (T28); every other worker is refused. Returns the value once, with when the staff app hides it again; the reveal is recorded and audited (who, when, which code; never the value). The response is never cached, never kept for idempotency and never logged. A removed code is not found. NOT_CONFIGURED while ACCESS_CODE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset. PROPOSED limit: 30 reveals per staff member per hour.

put.summary: Change a property’s address
put.description: Staff with customer.edit (Owner; Office with a reason). Records the next address version with its source and the required reason; the previous address stays as a former address, and every request keeps the address it was sent with. The coverage of the new ZIP is checked again (never blocking). If-Match is the property version.

post.summary: Record the verified address and county of a property
post.description: Staff with visit.confirm (Owner, Office). Records that staff checked the complete address of the current address version (addressChecked) and the county it lies in, with an optional note on how. The county is compared with the service area (coverage.area): inArea. A first visit is confirmed only after this, with the county inside the area; a later address change needs a new verification. If-Match is the property version; addressVersion must be the current one (ADDRESS_VERSION_CHANGED). The property version does not change.

put.summary: Record or clear a property detail
put.description: Staff with customer.edit (Owner; Office with a reason). The site contact and their authority, access windows, non-secret access instructions, parking and loading, occupants and pets, restricted areas, power and water access, customer preparation or known site flags, with its source and the required reason; null clears it (the history keeps it). Text that looks like an access code or a card number is refused: codes belong in the protected store. If-Match is the property version.

post.summary: Confirm a property detail is still right
post.description: Staff with customer.edit (Owner; Office with a reason). Records that the address, the type or a recorded detail was confirmed unchanged now, with its source and the required reason (DETAIL_NOT_RECORDED for a detail that holds nothing). If-Match is the property version.

put.summary: Verify a property’s time zone
put.description: TSK-0123 (OWN-DEC-159, HH-SCH-02): staff with customer.edit (Owner; Office with a reason) record the property’s IANA zone from the county of its verified address. The zone must be an Eastern or Central zone (read from the time-zone data, never a fixed offset): ZONE_NOT_SUPPORTED otherwise; when the configured county list (geo.county_time_zones) names the county with another zone, ZONE_COUNTY_MISMATCH. The zone history keeps every earlier state; the staff queue flag of an unknown zone resolves. Visits already planned keep the zone they were planned in. If-Match is the property version.

put.summary: Change a property’s type
put.description: Staff with customer.edit (Owner; Office with a reason). One of the property types of the request form (FACT-PROPERTY-TYPES), with its source and the required reason. If-Match is the property version.

post.description: Staff with fee.record (the Owner; Office PROPOSED). A Square fee in cents with its date, on a Square card payment (never cash, a check or another method) and/or the payout it was deducted in, and an optional reference. Never deducted from the customer payment: the payment stays as recorded (HH-FIN-06). Returns the payouts and fees.

get.description: The Owner (estimate.approve_publication). The approvals waiting for a decision, oldest first: the reference, the proposed price (and the highest total its options allow), the discount, change-order adjustments, the reasons approval is needed, the project documents counted together, the threshold and its version, the preparer and, from costs that exist only, the labor and material costs, gross profit and margin (none while the costs are incomplete). Integer cents.

The Owner (estimate.approve_publication). One approval record with what the Owner was shown and the decision: who, when, the comment and the document version; whether it was invalidated (a later change of price or scope) or used by the publication. ETag: the record version.

post.summary: Approve or reject publishing a document (Owner only)
post.description: The Owner only (estimate.approve_publication; OWN-DEC-173), with If-Match: the record version shown, and a written comment (the auditable reason, final owner amendments 2026-10-22). Only a pending approval is decided; one invalidated by a change of price or scope is refused. Records the decision, the time, the comment and the document version, and resolves the Owner Decisions item. An approval lets that exact version be published; any later change of price or scope invalidates it. Audited. Returns the record.

post.summary: Record the correction of a punch item
post.description: Staff with quality.correct_punch_item (the worker the item is assigned to, assigned to the job inside the access window), with If-Match: open -> corrected with what was done and the evidence. When no item stays open the review waits for the Owner's re-check.

Staff with quality.manage_punch_items (the Owner), with If-Match, on a corrected item: passed (rechecked) or failed (open again, the correction cleared; the note is kept in the history). Never by the person who corrected it, except on a self-review (RECHECKER_CORRECTED). A safety concern passes only once its safety hold is resolved (SAFETY_HOLD_UNRESOLVED). The last passed re-check passes the review and the job becomes operationally complete.

get.summary: Jobs awaiting quality review or with punch items
get.description: Staff with quality.review (the Owner). Every job awaiting quality review and every job with a punch item not re-checked (at most 200, by project reference): the review state, the punch items still to re-check (and how many are major) and the earliest due date.

Staff with request.view (a worker has My Day instead). Only the item types whose matrix action the caller holds are listed (own-record grants list only items assigned to the caller), filtered before ordering and paging. Ordered by urgency: safety, today’s appointment changes, overdue and other time-sensitive items, then by due time and age. Reasons that reveal restricted detail are replaced by a generic reason for roles that may not see it. No restricted field is stored on an item.

The Owner’s decisions waiting: deposit waivers, Start Work exceptions, refunds and cancellation outcomes, deletion requests, Overdue—owner decision invoices, damage, injury and dispute notifications. A caller without any of these grants is refused. Only the item types whose matrix action the caller holds are listed (own-record grants list only items assigned to the caller), filtered before ordering and paging. Ordered by urgency: safety, today’s appointment changes, overdue and other time-sensitive items, then by due time and age. Reasons that reveal restricted detail are replaced by a generic reason for roles that may not see it. No restricted field is stored on an item.

get.summary: Customer response: time to first meaningful response
get.description: The Owner (dashboard.view). For requests received in [from, to): how many were received, answered, awaiting and within the internal one-hour target, the share within target (basis points of requests whose outcome is known) and the average and median business minutes to the first meaningful response (OWN-DEC-125). Figures with nothing to measure are null (unavailable), never zero; requests whose clock was NOT CONFIGURED are counted apart. The Owner Dashboard (TSK-0096) reads it.

Staff with request.view (not workers). Requests newest first, filtered by state (open, closed or one state) and responsible staff member (me, unassigned or a staff id). Customer name, city, services and coverage only.

get.summary: A request: the original submission and its handling
get.description: Staff with request.view (not workers). The original request exactly as sent (services, answers, description, full address, timing, preferences, contact details), the contact verification badges (email and phone separately), coverage, the responsible staff member and reassignments, the latest qualification, internal notes (staff only), decisions with reasons, work packages, the next step, the follow-up due time and the actions the caller may take. The ETag is the request version for the actions’ If-Match. Photos are read from listRequestPhotos.

post.description: Staff with request.ask_question. Moves the request to "needs information" (from review, after a received request is moved to review). The questions themselves and their automatic notice are written and published with TSK-0051: no customer message is sent here; request.information_requested is recorded for it.

Staff with request.close_no_response (PROPOSED: the request-handling row), inside the caller’s scope (otherwise NOT_FOUND), with the request’s version (If-Match). Only an unbooked request waiting on the customer ("needs information") whose unanswered questions all had their final reminder actually sent (and still standing), at least the configured hours ago (reminders.cadences.unansweredQuestion.closeAfterFinalHours, 24, OWN-DEC-101). With accepted work, an appointment or money received it is refused (OWNER_REVIEW_REQUIRED): this rule never cancels accepted, scheduled or paid work. The request and project close with their history; open reminders are cancelled; a customer reply within the reopen period (request.reopen_period) reopens the same request. CONFLICT codes: INVALID_TRANSITION, NO_OPEN_QUESTION, FACTS_MISSING (a final reminder not sent), TOO_EARLY, CONFIG_MISSING, OWNER_REVIEW_REQUIRED.

Staff with request.choose_estimate_approach. "Site visit needed" with a short customer-facing explanation (OWN-DEC-99): needs the qualification recorded; creates one work package per listed service and moves the request to "needs site visit". Nothing is booked and no message is sent: the visit windows are offered with TSK-0063 (request.site_visit_required is recorded for it). Refused while a review hold is open or under review (REVIEW_HOLD_OPEN).

Staff with request.not_a_fit. Needs a reason category (coverage, outside our scope, specialist assessment needed, other) and the plain-language reason the customer sees; the internal note stays staff-only. With accepted work, an appointment or money received the project goes to the Owner for cancellation and financial review (Owner Decisions) and nothing closes; otherwise the request and project close with their history and decision.not_a_fit_published is recorded for the automatic notice.

Staff with request.choose_estimate_approach. "Estimate online": needs the qualification recorded; creates one work package per listed service of the one project and moves the request to "ready for estimate". The estimate itself is written with TSK-0052/TSK-0053; no message is sent. Refused while a review hold is open or under review (REVIEW_HOLD_OPEN).

Staff with request.record_conversation (PROPOSED: the request-handling row). A completed conversation with the customer (a logged phone call or a conversation in person) with its outcome, when it happened (default now; never before the request or in the future). Staff only. It is a meaningful response: the first one stops the first-response clock at the time it happened (OWN-DEC-116). Never edited or deleted.

post.summary: Add an internal note to a request
post.description: Staff with request.add_note (PROPOSED: the request-handling row). A staff-only note, kept separate from customer messages and never shown to customers. Notes are never edited or deleted; a correction is a new note. TSK-0044 (HH-STAFF-05): its visibility class is internal_operational unless restricted_incident (the Owner and the reporting worker only) or restricted_financial is chosen; never customer-shared. A card number is refused.

get.description: Staff (request.view). Every photo with its state; ready photos carry a signed URL valid for minutes. Quarantined and rejected photos are never served. TSK-0044 (HH-STAFF-05): a restricted photo is listed only for a role that reads its class (restricted incident: the Owner; restricted financial: the Owner).

put.summary: Record the qualification of a request
put.description: Staff with request.qualify (PROPOSED: the request-handling row). One outcome per check of HH-LEAD-02 (coverage, service fit, missing essential facts, urgency, site-visit need, staff and equipment, risk flags) with an optional note; each save is a new revision, and If-Match is the current revision (0 before the first). Classification is by staff; AI stays off. Never changes the request state or stops the clock. TSK-0043: risk flags needing attention name the potential hazards found (at least one, with a note); each newly named hazard opens a review hold in the same transaction. A later revision never clears a hold.

get.description: Staff with request.view, inside the caller’s scope (otherwise NOT_FOUND). The questions published in the request’s project, oldest first, each exactly as written with its author and time, its automatic notice (pending, sent, failed, with each delivery and Retry for a definite failure: a failed notice never starts the reminders), its one automatic reminder (TSK-0121: not scheduled, scheduled with the due time 3 days after the notice’s successful send, queued, sent, failed or cancelled, with each delivery; a text waits for the recipient’s permitted hours) and the customer’s reply exactly as written ("I’m not sure", the attached photos and their states, and whether it reopened the request). Also whether this caller may publish, whether replies wait for review, the configured cadence, whether "Closed—no response" is possible now (with the unmet requirements and when it becomes possible) and the reopen period.

post.summary: Publish a question to the customer
post.description: Staff with request.ask_question on the request, inside the caller’s scope (otherwise NOT_FOUND), with the request’s version (If-Match). Publishing is the release (OWN-DEC-98): the question is kept exactly as written (general, or a measurement the customer may answer "I’m not sure"), the request moves to "needs information" (a received request is moved to review first) or stays there, and question.published is recorded in the same transaction for the automatic notice "HandyHub has a question about your request. View and reply securely.", which links to the question through the project’s verified access. The staff member confirms the question never asks the customer to inspect a hazardous area (noHazardInspection). Card numbers are refused. Refused from any other state (CONFLICT INVALID_TRANSITION) or for a project that is not open (PROJECT_NOT_OPEN). The audit event never holds the text.

Staff with request.ask_question on the request, inside the caller’s scope (otherwise NOT_FOUND). Resolves the request’s "question replied" queue item (publishing another question, a request action or closing does the same). Nothing about the replies changes.

post.summary: Link a request to another customer
post.description: Staff with request.correct_link (Owner; Office with a reason and the preview): links the request, with its project, to an existing customer, or corrects a request linked to the wrong customer. A link, never a move: the request keeps its original submission and customer, and nothing is deleted. Requires the written reason and the confirmed preview digest (PREVIEW_STALE when anything changed since). Access is rechecked: the requester never gains the other customer’s projects, no grant or session gains a project, and a correction revokes the project’s guest links and sessions issued while the mistaken link stood. Only the Owner reverses it.

get.summary: Preview linking a request to another customer
get.description: Staff who may correct a request link (request.correct_link: Owner; Office with a reason and this preview). The request and its project, the customer it is linked to now and the one it would be linked to (`to`), each with contacts, properties and projects, documents and payments (not available in this release), and whether this corrects an earlier relink (a correction revokes the guest links and sessions of the project issued since that relink). Linking never gives the requester access to the other customer’s projects. `blocked` says why it cannot be confirmed now. The confirmation sends back `previewDigest`.

put.summary: Make one staff member responsible for a request
put.description: Staff with request.assign. Sets the one responsible staff member (an active staff member whose role may handle requests) on the request and its project; every reassignment is kept with who made it. If-Match is the request version; the new version is returned. Assigning never stops the first-response clock.

get.description: Staff with request.view (not workers). The request’s reference, status, submission time, service codes and responsible staff member; an unknown request answers NOT_FOUND. No contact or property detail.

get.summary: Who can be responsible for a request
get.description: Staff with request.assign. Active staff whose roles may handle requests (the matrix row "Ask a question, choose online or site visit, Not a Fit, assign responsible person"): id and name only.

get.summary: The retention schedule and the deletion-review queue
get.description: Owner only (ROLE-MATRIX retention.view). The retention schedule per category as configured (retention.*: the period, what starts it, the configuration version and its sources; OWN-DEC-70, OWN-DEC-142), whether the daily job can find the category’s records yet (scanned, start not recorded, no period), the last and next run, and how many entries wait for the Owner’s review.
